method: Rows 1-15 of ~/codewatch-research/gaps/misses.tsv in file order. The file held 59 missed cases, all cve-pairs-php (no Python, no JavaScript), and all were unread (rows 1-45 had been noted by the three earlier runs today, which the runner has removed). For each case I read the fix commit's message and full per-file diff (gh api repos/O/R/commits/SHA) and, where the diff did not show the source or the sink, the file at the fix commit's parent (gh api repos/O/R/contents/PATH?ref=PARENT, raw). Nothing was skipped.

notes.sink: url.php:27 window.location='" . htmlspecialchars($_GET['url']) . "'; inside an echoed <script> block (JavaScript string context, then window.location)

notes.source: wp-admin/includes/class-file-upload-upgrader.php:103 $this->filename = $_GET[$urlholder]; (GET parameter whose name is passed to the constructor, normally 'package')
notes.sink: wp-admin/includes/class-file-upload-upgrader.php:104 $this->package = $uploads['basedir'] . '/' . $this->filename; then :121 return @unlink( $this->package ); and the upgrader's install/unpack of that path
notes.between: the constructor takes $urlholder from its caller, checks only empty() and is_numeric() on the GET value, and in the back-compat branch concatenates it under wp_upload_dir()['basedir']; the traversal (../../wp-config.php) is carried in the public $package property and used by cleanup() here and by the upgrade functions in other files; the property hop is what hides the flow.
notes.fix: applies sanitize_file_name() to the GET value and refuses a realpath outside the uploads basedir
notes.probe:
<?php
class File_Upload_Upgrader {
    public $package;
    public $filename;
    public function __construct( $form, $urlholder ) {
        $uploads = wp_upload_dir();
        $this->filename = $_GET[ $urlholder ];
        $this->package = $uploads['basedir'] . '/' . $this->filename;
    }
    public function cleanup() {
        if ( file_exists( $this->package ) ) {
            return @unlink( $this->package );
        }
        return true;
    }
}

notes.source: index.php:293 $filename = isset($_REQUEST[$request]) ? trim($_REQUEST[$request]) : false; (the deleteFile / deleteTheme / deletePlugin parameter; $request is the parameter name from the list at :286-290)
notes.sink: index.php:303 wCMS::recursiveDelete("{$folder}/{$filename}"); which at :587-594 recurses with glob() and calls rmdir() / unlink()
notes.between: wCMS::$loggedIn and a hash_equals() token gate the action; the only value check is that the name is not the active theme at :297, with no containment test, so a deleteFile such as ../../database.js is concatenated onto __DIR__.'/files' and handed to the class's own recursiveDelete(), which recursively removes directories and files. The request superglobal with a variable key and the project delete helper are two hops from the actual rmdir()/unlink().
notes.fix: resolves realpath() of the base and of the target and proceeds only when the target lies inside the base directory
notes.probe:
<?php
class FileManager {
    public static function deleteFiles() {
        foreach ( array( array( __DIR__ . '/files', 'deleteFile' ), array( __DIR__ . '/themes', 'deleteTheme' ) ) as $entry ) {
            list( $folder, $request ) = $entry;
            $filename = isset( $_REQUEST[$request] ) ? trim( $_REQUEST[$request] ) : false;
            if ( !$filename || empty( $filename ) ) { continue; }
            if ( file_exists( "{$folder}/{$filename}" ) ) {
                self::recursiveDelete( "{$folder}/{$filename}" );
            }
        }
    }
    private static function recursiveDelete( $file ) {
        if ( is_dir( $file ) ) {
            foreach ( glob( $file . '*' ) as $dir ) { self::recursiveDelete( $dir ); }
            rmdir( $file );
        } elseif ( is_file( $file ) ) {
            unlink( $file );
        }
    }
}
